The 7B2 mAb bound to the epitope analyzed by surface plasmon resonance. MAb 7B2 also recognized the overlapping peptides DQQLLGIWGCSGKLI, LLGIWGCSGKLICTT, IWGCSGKLICTTAVP, and CSGKLICTTAVPWNA  and showed cross-clade reactivity (clades A, B, C, D, CRF1 and CRF2) in a peptide microarray used to map the epitope. Alanine substitutions demonstrated that residues Cys598, Gly600, Leu602 and Ile603 were critical for binding. Ala substitution of Cys604 resulted in a peptide that bound with a higher peak response, yet had an off-rate approximately 2.8 times that of the Cys604 peptide. The authors postulated that Cys604 mediated cyclization of the peptide that would be critical for the generation of a stable 7B2-peptide complex, which was supported by the observed 100 to 150 fold increased off rates in reducing conditions.

The HIV-1 gp120 core contains truncations in the variable V1/V2 and V3 loops as well as the N- and C-termini. The structure of epitope-specific antibody CH235 bound to the HIV-1 Env trimer was determined by negative stain EM. The 3-D reconstructions of Fabs CH235, CH235.9 and CH235.12 bound to trimeric BG505 and B41 HIV-1 Env glycoprotein showed that the stoichiometry increased with antibody maturation. CH235 bound with a stoichiometry of 1:1 or 2:1 Fabs per trimer and CH235.9 and CH235.12 bound stoichiometry of 3:1 Fab to trimer ratio.

The epitope-specific antibody CH235 was tested by ELISA for binding to 113 recombinant CH505 gp120 Env isolated from time of transmission to week 160 post-transmission, including CH505 TF loop D mutant Envs and 15 heterologous gp120 Envs. Of note, CH235.9 and CH235.12 bound to 4/22 and 8/22 Envs isolated from week 136 and 160 post-transmission, respectively. The affinity of epitope-specific antibody CH235 lineage for binding to HIV-1 CH505 TF Env increased four orders of magnitude during affinity maturation, as determined by surface plasmon resonance.
